subject: Computer Networking
title: The Internet vs. The Web
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on The Internet vs. The Web.

hook.text: People use 'internet' and 'web' interchangeably. They're actually two different things.

buildup.text: The internet is the global network — cables, routers, protocols. It existed before the web.

discovery.text: The web is a service on the internet. It uses HTTP to deliver pages linked by hyperlinks. Invented in 1991.

twist.text: Email, FTP, gaming, streaming — these all use the internet but are not the web.

climax.text: Tim Berners-Lee created the web at CERN. His first browser was also an editor — he imagined a read-write web.

punchline.text: The internet is the road. The web is one vehicle on it.

quiz.question: What is the relationship between the internet and the web?
options: The web is a service that runs on the internet
They are the same thing with different names
The internet was invented after the web

details.summary: The internet is the global network of networks connected by cables and protocols. The World Wide Web is one service running on the internet, using HTTP and browsers to deliver linked documents. Email, streaming, gaming, and messaging also run on the internet but are separate from the web.
details.whyItMatters: Confusing the internet with the web is the most common networking misconception. Understanding the distinction clarifies the architecture of our connected world.
takeaways: The internet is the physical and logical network infrastructure
The web is one application running on top of the internet
Email, streaming, and gaming are internet services but not the web

faq.question: When was the web created and by whom?
faq.answer: Tim Berners-Lee invented the World Wide Web in 1989 at CERN. He created HTML, HTTP, and the first web browser and server. The web was built on top of the existing internet, which had been operating since the 1980s with email and file transfer already in use.

faq.question: Can the internet exist without the web?
faq.answer: Yes. The internet existed for decades before the web. Email was invented in the 1970s, file transfer in the 1980s. If the web disappeared, the internet would continue carrying email, streaming, messaging, and other services. The web is the internet's most popular application.
